source: MAFF — សារៈប្រយោជន៍នៃដំណាំស្រូវ (Value of the Rice Crop) slide deck, presenter contact temseng@yahoo.com, p.13
text: Rice and rice byproducts can be processed into cosmetic and personal-care products, presented on the slide under a 'Cosmetics' category with four sub-types: (1) Powder — rice-starch-based body/baby powder, illustrated with a commercial 'Johnson's Baby Powder' bottle used as a reference example and with 'ReisCare Baby Powder' products explicitly marketed as biodegradable and talc-free; (2) Lotion and Moisturizer; (3) Kojic Acid — a compound used as an active ingredient in skin-whitening creams; (4) Rice peptides — marketed as protecting skin from collagen degradation (an anti-aging claim). Additional example products shown include an 'Angel Rice' brand rice-germ/vitamin cream and lotion line, and a 'White Jasmine Rice Soap' bar soap branded around jasmine rice. Together these illustrate a rice-derived cosmetics/personal-care value chain — distinct from food products — targeting beauty and skincare markets, which could represent a higher-margin outlet for rice starch, rice bran, or rice extracts.
